name: Algorithmic stablecoin
durability: Only as durable as the peg-keeping algorithm and market confidence — Terra/UST's 2022 collapse shows this isn't guaranteed.
portability: Fully portable — transfers at blockchain speed anywhere with network access.
acceptability: Narrow and volatility-dependent — accepted within DeFi contexts, not a stable general medium.
desc: Programmatic peg-keeper; market-game preserved beneath a stability layer.
panelDesc: Holds its peg through code, not reserves: contracts algorithmically expand or shrink supply to keep price stable, with no fiat backing behind the token.
g1_gamepos: Accepts the existing game; adds programmatic stability layer
g1_valuesignal: Single rational unit pegged to fiat reference; price-mediated
g1_accumulation: Enables accumulation; subject to fiat-equivalent inflation losses
g1_divisibility: Infinitely divisible like its fiat peg; smallest unit set by the token's decimal precision.
g1_uniformity: Every unit fungible — algorithmically pegged to track a stable reference value.
g2_coordination: Price-aggregation plus algorithmic peg-maintenance
g2_governance: Algorithmic issuance; governance via DAO or sponsor org
g2_scale: Global from inception; no federation logic
g3_ethic: Smithian; self-interest channeled through stability
g3_accumdrive: Drive accepted; should be channeled productively
g3_status: Encoded in monetary signal
g3_time: Short — no intrinsic value, code-backed and easily traded, with no architectural connection to anything durable.
trackRecord: Terra/UST scaled to tens of billions in market cap before its algorithmic peg collapsed in May 2022, wiping out most of its value within days — the most consequential real-world test of this design to date.
governanceRequirements: Protocol-level governance only (typically a foundation or DAO controlling the peg mechanism) — no requirement on the end user beyond holding the token.
resourceRequirements: None beyond a crypto wallet and the stablecoin itself; issuing a new one requires substantial smart-contract and reserve-management infrastructure.

name: Asset-backed digital stablecoin
durability: Durable as long as the reserve custodian stays solvent and redemption holds — audits are the real constraint.
portability: Fully portable — blockchain-speed transfers globally.
acceptability: Broad within crypto/DeFi rails and growing in payments, though not legal tender anywhere.
desc: Reserve-backed digital dollar; market-game preserved with added convertibility.
panelDesc: Backs each token one-to-one with real reserve assets — cash, bonds, or similar — redeemable on demand, so trust in solvency keeps the price stable.
g1_gamepos: Accepts the existing game; adds digital liquidity layer
g1_valuesignal: Single rational unit backed by reserve assets; price-mediated
g1_accumulation: Enables accumulation; backing assets may appreciate or depreciate
g1_divisibility: Infinitely divisible; decimal precision matches the reserve-backed peg.
g1_uniformity: Fully fungible — each unit is an interchangeable claim on the same reserve pool.
g2_coordination: Price-aggregation plus reserve-backed convertibility
g2_governance: Centralized issuer with reserve attestation
g2_scale: Global from inception; no federation logic
g3_ethic: Smithian; reserve-backed stability as trust substitute
g3_accumdrive: Drive accepted; should be channeled productively
g3_status: Encoded in monetary signal
g3_time: Short — redeemable for cash or bonds, liquid financial instruments rather than durable goods or precious metals.
trackRecord: USDC and Tether together represent well over $100B in circulating supply and are widely used across crypto exchanges and increasingly in payments — the most successful real-world deployment among the reference points here.
governanceRequirements: Held by a centralized issuer (Circle, Tether) who manages reserves and redemption — end users need no governance structure of their own, just an account with the issuer or an exchange.
resourceRequirements: A crypto wallet and, for redemption at par, an account with the issuer; issuing a new asset-backed stablecoin requires substantial reserve capital and regulatory compliance infrastructure.

name: Bank-issued credit money
durability: Durable in aggregate via the banking system, though any single bank's credit is only as durable as that bank's solvency.
portability: Highly portable via modern payment rails — wires, cards, transfers.
acceptability: Near-universal within its issuing jurisdiction — the default medium of exchange.
desc: The constituting form of the modern monetary game — debt-based, bank-issued.
panelDesc: Created the moment a bank extends a loan, expanding the money supply through bookkeeping. Reserve rules and interest-rate policy constrain how much banks can create.
g1_gamepos: Accepts and constitutes the existing game
g1_valuesignal: Single rational unit; price-aggregation through markets
g1_accumulation: Enables accumulation; subject to inflation-targeting policy
g1_divisibility: Divisible to the cent, same granularity as the fiat it's denominated in.
g1_uniformity: Fully fungible — one dollar of credit is interchangeable with any other.
g2_coordination: Price-aggregation through markets
g2_governance: Commercial banks issue against collateral; state-regulated
g2_scale: National scale typically; transnational through correspondent banking
g3_ethic: Hobbesian-Smithian; privately issued through voluntary lending relationships (Smithian), but constrained by state-set reserve requirements and interest-rate policy — a real institutional check on otherwise market-driven issuance (Hobbesian).
g3_accumdrive: Drive accepted; channeled through interest-bearing instruments
g3_status: Encoded in monetary signal
g3_time: Short — debt-based and discounting-driven, with no durable anchor behind the credit it issues.
trackRecord: The default form of money creation in every modern economy — trillions in outstanding bank credit globally, continuously since the rise of fractional-reserve banking [a].
governanceRequirements: None for an individual or business using it — governance sits entirely with licensed banks and central-bank regulators.
resourceRequirements: A bank account and creditworthiness; nothing else.

name: Commodity-backed money
durability: Very high — physical commodities like gold are chemically stable and don't degrade.
portability: Low — weight and bulk make large transactions physically cumbersome, the historical reason paper claims emerged.
acceptability: Historically near-universal; today mostly reserve-only, not circulating.
desc: Pre-fiat reference: scarcity anchored to a physical thing.
panelDesc: Ties the unit of account to a fixed quantity of a physical good, so money's value rests on real scarcity rather than institutional promise.
g1_gamepos: Accepts the game; anchors it to physical scarcity
g1_valuesignal: Single rational unit anchored to physical commodity
g1_accumulation: Enables accumulation; commodity scarcity disciplines supply
g1_divisibility: Divisible in principle (coinage, fractional weights), though physical splitting has practical limits paper claims solved historically.
g1_uniformity: Fungible once refined to a standard purity — an ounce of gold is any ounce of gold.
g2_coordination: Price-aggregation plus commodity reserve
g2_governance: Variable; historically state or private banks issued
g2_scale: National to transnational; gold-standard federation pattern
g3_ethic: Smithian — no legal-tender mandate or state-set policy at all; the commodity's own market activity sets its worth directly, without institutional backing or constraint.
g3_accumdrive: Drive accepted; commodity scarcity disciplines accumulation
g3_status: Encoded in monetary signal
g3_time: Tied to a precious metal — durable, but not automatically long-horizon.
trackRecord: Millennia of real-world use as money; the Bretton Woods gold-exchange standard operated from 1944 to 1971 before being abandoned in favor of pure fiat.
governanceRequirements: None for holding or trading the commodity itself; historically required a central bank or treasury to maintain convertibility.
resourceRequirements: Physical storage and security for the commodity itself, or a custodian/vault relationship.

name: Cryptographically scarce digital commodity money
durability: High for as long as the network's nodes and miners keep participating — no physical decay, but durability is contingent, not absolute.
portability: Fully portable — a private key moves any amount anywhere instantly.
acceptability: Broad and growing but narrower than fiat — merchant acceptance varies widely by jurisdiction.
desc: Engineered scarcity replaces sovereign issuance; market-game intensified.
panelDesc: Caps total issuance on a fixed, verifiable schedule enforced by proof-of-work rather than any authority — scarcity is absolute and permanent.
g1_gamepos: Replaces sovereign issuance; preserves market-game structure
g1_valuesignal: Single rational unit; engineered absolute scarcity
g1_accumulation: Enables extreme accumulation via deflationary dynamics
g1_divisibility: Divisible to 100 million satoshis per coin — engineered fine-grained divisibility.
g1_uniformity: Fungible in protocol terms, though chain-analysis can make individual coins traceable in practice.
g2_coordination: Price-aggregation through speculative markets
g2_governance: Algorithmic issuance schedule; no governance after design
g2_scale: Global from inception; no federation; single chain
g3_ethic: Hobbesian-Smithian; assumes rivalry and deflation as the natural state (Hobbesian), realized through ordinary voluntary market exchange with no institutional enforcer (Smithian) — fixed supply and proof-of-work make scarcity structural, not policy-set.
g3_accumdrive: Drive maximized; deflation rewards accumulation absolutely
g3_status: Encoded intensely in monetary signal
g3_time: Short — a scarce, easily-traded asset with no architectural connection to anything durable ('digital gold' is analogy, not design).
trackRecord: Continuously operating since the 2009 genesis block [a], now with a market capitalization in the trillions and adoption ranging from individual holders to national reserves (e.g. El Salvador).
governanceRequirements: None to hold or transact — governance is protocol-level (miner/node consensus), entirely outside any individual holder's control.
resourceRequirements: A wallet (software or hardware) and, to transact, some BTC and awareness of network fees; mining requires substantial specialized hardware and electricity.

name: Fiat sovereign currency
durability: Institutionally durable via sovereign continuity — worn notes are reissued without any loss of value.
portability: Highly portable via modern banking and payment infrastructure; cash itself travels in small amounts too.
acceptability: Universal within its issuing jurisdiction by legal-tender mandate — the baseline every other mechanism here is compared against.
desc: State-issued, central-bank-governed; the constituting form of the modern game.
panelDesc: Backed by government decree and taxing power rather than a physical anchor, with a central bank managing supply through interest-rate policy.
g1_gamepos: Accepts and constitutes the existing game
g1_valuesignal: Single rational unit; price-aggregation through markets
g1_accumulation: Enables accumulation; subject to inflation-targeting policy
g1_divisibility: Divisible to the smallest denominated unit (cents), matching conventional market expectations.
g1_uniformity: Fully fungible — the defining property of legal-tender currency.
g2_coordination: Price-aggregation through markets
g2_governance: State monopoly issuance; central bank governance
g2_scale: National with international clearing through reserve currencies
g3_ethic: Hobbesian-Smithian; ordinary market exchange (Smithian) backed by real state coercion — legal tender laws and tax obligations guarantee demand independent of market consensus (Hobbesian).
g3_accumdrive: Drive accepted; channeled through monetary policy
g3_status: Encoded in monetary signal
g3_time: Short — discounting-driven, with no durable anchor behind the currency.
trackRecord: The universal, continuously operating baseline for the modern global economy — every sovereign nation issues one.
governanceRequirements: None for an individual using it; governance sits with the issuing central bank and treasury.
resourceRequirements: None beyond ordinary access to banking or cash — the baseline every other mechanism here is compared against.

name: Programmable central bank digital currency
durability: Same institutional durability as fiat, though the digital infrastructure itself is a new failure surface.
portability: Highly portable digitally, though transfers may be programmatically restricted (expiry, geofencing) by design.
acceptability: Legal-tender status in principle, though real rollouts (e.g. e-CNY) show adoption lagging behind the mandate.
desc: Programmable fiat: the sovereign's monetary reach extends into every transaction, balance, and expiry date.
panelDesc: A sovereign digital currency where the central bank programs rules into the money itself — expiry, spending limits, transfer conditions.
g1_gamepos: Accepts the existing game; digitizes sovereign issuance and adds a programmable constraint layer
g1_valuesignal: Single rational unit; programmable rules govern transfer, expiry, and conditional spending
g1_accumulation: Variable by design; can be programmed to enable, penalize, or conditionally restrict accumulation
g1_divisibility: Divisible to the smallest programmable unit, same as the fiat it digitizes.
g1_uniformity: Nominally fungible, though programmable rules (expiry, use-restrictions) can make specific units behave differently in practice.
g2_coordination: Price-aggregation plus algorithmic-mechanism-design; the sovereign encodes behavioral rules directly into the currency
g2_governance: Central bank issues; state programs and enforces behavioral constraints on balances
g2_scale: National typically; cross-border through bilateral or multilateral CBDC bridge protocols
g3_ethic: Hobbesian; assumes citizens require sovereign oversight and discipline to coordinate exchange safely
g3_accumdrive: Variable; programmable expiry, spending caps, or conditional-use restrictions at sovereign discretion
g3_status: Encoded in monetary signal; full transaction visibility extends the state's disciplinary reach
g3_time: Short — programmable expiry actively enforces short-term spending at the sovereign’s discretion.
trackRecord: Live pilots are underway in multiple jurisdictions — China's e-CNY and Sweden's e-krona are the best-documented — but no major economy has fully replaced cash with a CBDC yet [a].
governanceRequirements: None for an individual user; governance sits entirely with the issuing central bank, which also sets the programmable rules.
resourceRequirements: A digital wallet compatible with the issuing central bank's system; issuing one requires substantial state-level digital infrastructure.

name: Agent-centric currency framework
durability: Not fixed at the framework level — durability depends entirely on which currency app is built on the substrate.
portability: Not fixed at the framework level — the substrate imposes no distance constraint itself; app-dependent.
acceptability: Undefined at the substrate level — acceptability belongs to whatever currency is actually built on it.
desc: Substrate, not currency: lets each agent define and validate its own units.
panelDesc: Not a currency itself but a substrate letting any community define and cryptographically validate its own currency rules without a shared global ledger.
g1_gamepos: Modifies the game; substrate for plural mechanisms
g1_valuesignal: Multiple units per agent permitted; richness depends on app
g1_accumulation: Depends on currency design; framework imposes no regime
g1_divisibility: Divisibility isn't fixed by the substrate — each currency app built on it sets its own granularity.
g1_uniformity: Fungibility isn't fixed by the substrate either — depends entirely on the app's own design.
g2_coordination: Tacit-emergent at protocol level; primary mechanism depends on app
g2_governance: Per-agent issuance with cryptographic validation; no global consensus
g2_scale: Local-first; scales through agent connectivity; federation native
g3_ethic: Smithian by default; the framework itself imposes no assumption about human nature — the taxonomy's default reading for architecture that doesn't engage the question.
g3_accumdrive: Depends on currency designed atop the framework
g3_status: Depends on currency design; framework supports separation
g3_time: Variable — a pure substrate that lets each agent define and validate its own currency rules; the framework itself takes no position on time horizon.
trackRecord: The Holochain framework has been live since 2018, with several currency apps built on it (e.g. early HoloFuel testnets) [a], but no single agent-centric currency has yet reached mainstream adoption at the scale of established cryptocurrencies.
governanceRequirements: Depends entirely on the specific app built on the substrate — the framework itself imposes none.
resourceRequirements: Running a Holochain node is modest (laptop-class hardware, unlike blockchain mining); building a new currency app requires development expertise.

name: Antirival accounting
durability: Not a stored-value question — value lives in ongoing shared use, not in a durable token.
portability: Doesn't transport in the usual sense — sharing rights propagate through use, not by moving a token between holders.
acceptability: Narrow — a specific-community experiment (Aalto/ECSA sNFTs), not designed for broad exchange.
desc: Units that gain value with shared use — sharing replaces exchange.
panelDesc: Inverts ordinary scarcity economics: units gain value the more people share and use them, rather than representing a claim on something finite.
g1_gamepos: Replaces exchange-logic with sharing-logic for specific goods
g1_valuesignal: Multiple antirival units; value increases with shared use
g1_accumulation: Accumulation undefined; sharing is the fundamental operation
g1_divisibility: Doesn't operate on a divisible scalar at all — sharing rights aren't a quantity that splits.
g1_uniformity: Explicitly non-fungible by design — sNFT-based, each unit carries unique sharing-rights identity.
g2_coordination: Deliberative; valuation through shared-use signals
g2_governance: Community-issued sNFTs; rules per community
g2_scale: Application-scale; federation logic underdeveloped
g3_ethic: Rousseauian; assumes generosity in shared use
g3_accumdrive: Drive reframed; value grows through giving not taking
g3_status: Separated from monetary signal through plural units
g3_time: Long — value accretes through sharing and commons use, a form of durability extended to the commons itself rather than a single durable asset.
trackRecord: Remains at the academic/experimental stage — the Aalto University and ECSA sNFT research has produced working prototypes [a] but no wide-scale real-world deployment yet.
governanceRequirements: Informal community agreement on what counts as legitimate sharing; no formal legal entity required for the experiments run so far.
resourceRequirements: A blockchain or ledger platform capable of issuing sNFTs; otherwise no special infrastructure.

name: Bioregional ecological-impact-backed currency
durability: The token itself is digitally durable, but its value anchor (ecological health) can degrade if the underlying ecosystem does.
portability: Digitally portable, but deliberately place-bound in spirit — its value signal is meant to stay tied to one bioregion.
acceptability: Narrow by design — accepted within a specific bioregional market (BioFi), not meant to circulate globally.
desc: Value indexed to bioregional ecological measures; capital flows where regeneration shows.
panelDesc: Pegs issuance to measurable ecological outcomes within a bioregion, so capital flows only where soil, water, or biodiversity demonstrably improve.
g1_gamepos: Modifies the game; channels capital to regenerative projects
g1_valuesignal: Single rational unit indexed to bioregional ecological measures
g1_accumulation: Enables accumulation but tied to regenerative-asset performance
g1_divisibility: Finely divisible like conventional currency, despite being indexed to ecological measures.
g1_uniformity: Fungible — an ordinary interchangeable token, just value-anchored to bioregional health.
g2_coordination: Algorithmic-mechanism-design indexed to ecological measures
g2_governance: Bioregional institution issues; community-bioregion governance
g2_scale: Bioregional with potential for bioregion-to-bioregion federation
g3_ethic: Smithian-Rousseauian; assumes ordinary self-interest alongside a genuine capacity for bioregional stewardship.
g3_accumdrive: Drive accepted but tied to regenerative-asset performance
g3_status: Partially encoded; partially separated through impact metrics
g3_time: Long — anchored to ecological restoration, the kind of long-term societal end the axis names directly.
trackRecord: BioFi and similar bioregional-finance initiatives are early-stage [a], with pilot projects in specific bioregions but not yet a track record of sustained, scaled operation.
governanceRequirements: Typically requires a bioregional stewardship body or cooperative empowered to define and verify the ecological measures the currency is indexed to.
resourceRequirements: Ecological monitoring/verification infrastructure for the region, plus a digital ledger to issue and track the currency.

name: Bonding curve / continuous token
durability: Durable as long as the smart contract and its treasury persist — no physical decay, but contract risk is real.
portability: Fully portable — a standard transferable token.
acceptability: Narrow — accepted within the specific community whose treasury backs it.
desc: Curve-mediated mint/burn around a community treasury — a warm currency.
panelDesc: Mints and burns tokens continuously along a mathematical price curve tied to a shared treasury, encoding community values into the math itself.
g1_gamepos: Modifies the game; warm currency with semi-permeable membrane
g1_valuesignal: Single rational unit; algorithmic price discovery
g1_accumulation: Enables accumulation; rules encoded in curve mathematics
g1_divisibility: Finely divisible — the continuous bonding curve mints/burns at arbitrary precision.
g1_uniformity: Fungible — a standard interchangeable token traded against the curve.
g2_coordination: Algorithmic-mechanism-design with bonding-curve price discovery
g2_governance: Community DAO issues against curve; mathematics encodes rules
g2_scale: Community-scale; federation rare; designed for single commons
g3_ethic: Smithian-Rousseauian; warm currency embeds community values alongside ordinary market self-interest.
g3_accumdrive: Drive accepted but bounded by curve mathematics
g3_status: Mixed; depends on community values encoded in curve
g3_time: Mid-range by design — a treasury-anchored curve, neither purely short-term trading nor a long-horizon commitment.
trackRecord: Augmented bonding curves have been used by several DAOs and community projects (e.g. Giveth) [a] to fund treasuries, with real but modest amounts raised — a proven pattern at community scale, not yet at large scale.
governanceRequirements: A community or DAO to define curve parameters and govern the treasury the curve mints against.
resourceRequirements: Smart-contract deployment on a blockchain and initial treasury capital to seed the curve.

name: Calculation-in-kind
durability: Varies entirely by physical good — grain and machinery have wildly different shelf lives; exactly why this mechanism sits outside the radar chart.
portability: Varies entirely by physical good — some goods transport easily, others not at all.
acceptability: Historically narrow (centrally planned economies) — no market-based acceptance mechanism exists at all, by design.
desc: No common scalar — physical units accounted natively, production for use.
panelDesc: Abandons a common monetary unit entirely, planning and allocating goods in their own physical measures, as Soviet-era Gosplan attempted.
g1_gamepos: Replaces money entirely with disaggregated physical accounting
g1_valuesignal: Multiple physical units in their native magnitudes; no common scalar
g1_accumulation: Accumulation undefined; goods are produced for use not exchange
g1_divisibility: Depends entirely on the physical good — grain divides finely, a tractor doesn't divide at all.
g1_uniformity: Depends entirely on the physical good — identical grain units are fungible, unique machinery is not.
g2_coordination: Deliberative central planning; no price mechanism
g2_governance: State or commune authority allocates physical units
g2_scale: National or commune-scale; federation logic underspecified
g3_ethic: Rousseauian; assumes capacity for cooperative planning
g3_accumdrive: Drive treated as institutional artifact; designed out
g3_status: Designed out; production is for use not signaling
g3_time: Long — oriented toward explicit collective, civilizational-scale planning.
trackRecord: Soviet Gosplan-style calculation-in-kind was run at national scale for decades (1920s-1991) [a] — a real, large-scale historical track record, though one widely judged to have produced significant inefficiencies. Discontinued with the Soviet collapse; not operating anywhere today at that scale.
governanceRequirements: Requires a central planning authority with the power to allocate physical goods directly — the most institutionally demanding governance requirement in this dataset.
resourceRequirements: Comprehensive production and logistics data systems capable of tracking physical goods at the granularity being planned.

name: Capped-return / purpose capital
durability: Durable as a contractual equity claim for as long as the venture operates.
portability: Portable as a financial instrument via standard share transfer, though typically illiquid — no public market.
acceptability: Narrow — accepted only among impact investors who accept the capped-return structure, not a general medium.
desc: Investor returns capped at a multiple; surplus flows back to the commons.
panelDesc: Lets investors earn returns up to a set multiple of their stake, after which further surplus redirects back to the enterprise's mission.
g1_gamepos: Modifies the game; redirects surplus after defined cap
g1_valuesignal: Single rational unit but with capped-claim structure
g1_accumulation: Enables time-bounded accumulation; surplus redirects to commons
g1_divisibility: Divisible like conventional equity — shares split to arbitrary precision.
g1_uniformity: Fungible within a share class, despite the capped-return structure limiting upside.
g2_coordination: Price-aggregation at entry; algorithmic-cap at exit
g2_governance: Investment vehicle structure; governance via redemption rules
g2_scale: Firm-scale typically; portfolio federation through fund-of-funds
g3_ethic: Smithian-Rousseauian; assumes capacity for fair-but-bounded enrichment — self-interest capped by a fairness norm.
g3_accumdrive: Drive accepted but capped at defined multiple
g3_status: Partially encoded for capped period; redirected to commons
g3_time: Long — surplus is redirected to the commons rather than extracted, a direct institutional-stability orientation.
trackRecord: Steward-ownership and capped-return structures have a real but still-niche track record — dozens of companies (documented by Purpose Foundation, Zebras Unite, and similar networks) [a] have adopted the model, mostly small-to-mid-size businesses.
governanceRequirements: Requires a formal legal entity (typically a company with a purpose-trust or golden-share structure) to enforce the capped-return terms.
resourceRequirements: Legal setup costs to establish the steward-ownership structure; otherwise the same working capital any business needs.

name: Carbon-sequestration-backed token
durability: Digitally durable as a token, but its backing (verified carbon removal) depends on measurement infrastructure staying credible.
portability: Fully portable digitally, same as any tokenized asset.
acceptability: Narrow — accepted within carbon-market participants (Regen Network/NCT), not a general medium of exchange.
desc: Unit anchored to verified carbon removal — habitability as the reserve asset.
panelDesc: Anchors a token's value to independently verified carbon sequestration, so habitability itself — not currency or debt — backs the money.
g1_gamepos: Modifies the game; anchors unit of account to global habitability
g1_valuesignal: Single rational unit pegged to verified bio-sequestration
g1_accumulation: Enables accumulation tied to demonstrated carbon removal
g1_divisibility: Finely divisible — verified carbon removal is tokenized down to fractional units.
g1_uniformity: Fungible — one verified ton of sequestration is interchangeable with any other.
g2_coordination: Algorithmic-mechanism-design with verified-sequestration backing
g2_governance: Multi-issuer with verification protocols
g2_scale: Global from inception; verification networks federate
g3_ethic: Smithian-Rousseauian; assumes ordinary self-interest alongside a genuine capacity for planetary stewardship.
g3_accumdrive: Drive accepted but tied to global habitability index
g3_status: Partially encoded; partially separated through habitability tie
g3_time: Long — anchored to carbon removal, the kind of long-term ecological end the axis names directly.
trackRecord: Carbon-market tokenization (Regen Network, Toucan/NCT, and similar) [a] has moved real capital — hundreds of millions of dollars in tokenized carbon credits — though the space has also seen credible-verification controversies.
governanceRequirements: Requires a verification/registry body (or reliance on an existing one like Verra) to certify the underlying carbon-removal claims.
resourceRequirements: Access to verified carbon-removal projects and measurement infrastructure, plus a blockchain platform to tokenize the credits.

name: Commitment pooling
durability: Not applicable — commitments are fulfilled and retired, not held as a durable store.
portability: Registries federate, so commitments can move between pools, but they aren't 'spent' the way currency is.
acceptability: Narrow — accepted within specific trust networks (Trustlines-style), inherently relational rather than universal.
desc: Commitments — not balances — as the primary unit; registries federate pools.
panelDesc: Treats promises between parties, not currency balances, as the thing actually tracked and cleared across a federating network of pools.
g1_gamepos: Modifies the game; commitments as primary unit, not money
g1_valuesignal: Plural commitment types valued numerically or relationally
g1_accumulation: Accumulation governed by registry rules and swap limiters
g1_divisibility: Commitments aren't a divisible quantity — each one is a discrete, specific promise.
g1_uniformity: Non-fungible by nature — plural commitment types, each specific to its own promise.
g2_coordination: Deliberative with registry/index/limiter/treasury functions
g2_governance: Per-pool stewardship with cross-pool federation
g2_scale: Designed for federation; pools confederate through registries
g3_ethic: Rousseauian; assumes capacity for promise-keeping — cooperation as the human default, not a self-interest-plus-virtue blend.
g3_accumdrive: Drive moderated through registry rules and swap limiters
g3_status: Separated from monetary signal through plural commitment types
g3_time: Variable — a substrate of commitments and registries cleared regardless of duration, with no inherent time orientation of its own.
trackRecord: Trustlines and similar commitment-pooling registries [a] remain niche, with real but small deployments — not yet a track record of scaled adoption.
governanceRequirements: Requires a trust network or registry maintaining the commitments — typically informal among known participants, formalized as the network grows.
resourceRequirements: A ledger/registry system to track commitments; no capital reserve required since nothing is minted against collateral.

name: Cooperative-work issuance
durability: Ledger entries persist, but gaining new value requires ongoing multi-agent co-signing (Proof-of-Integration) — durable record, not durable exchangeability.
portability: Holonically nested within the AD4M/Holochain community — not designed to move outside that specific structure.
acceptability: Very narrow — accepted only within the specific cooperative issuing it (Synergy).
desc: Value requires multi-agent co-signed cooperation (Proof-of-Integration); holonic personal and organ currencies on AD4M/Holochain.
panelDesc: Mints personal and community currencies only when multiple agents co-sign completed cooperative work, making solo value-creation impossible.
g1_gamepos: Replaces scarcity-logic; no value is created without multi-agent co-signed cooperative work
g1_valuesignal: Personal tokens per agent and organ currencies per community; holonically nested
g1_accumulation: Variable; tokens mintable only through co-signed work; redeemable to contributors' original commitments
g1_divisibility: Personal and organ tokens aren't a divisible common scalar — each is tied to specific contributions.
g1_uniformity: Non-fungible — tokens are holonically tied to specific contributor commitments, not interchangeable.
g2_coordination: Deliberative; Proof-of-Integration requires explicit multi-agent co-signing for every unit issued
g2_governance: Membrane-defined community boundaries; organ governance at each holonic level
g2_scale: Variable; holonic nesting spans personal → organ → meta-organ levels with cross-membrane value flow
g3_ethic: Rousseauian; cooperation is structurally required to produce any value — solo action yields nothing
g3_accumdrive: Integration-oriented; solo accumulation blocked at the protocol level
g3_status: Partially separated; tokens remain traceable to specific contributors and their commitments
g3_time: Long — built on multi-agent cooperative commitments and holonic governance, oriented toward institutional and cooperative durability.
trackRecord: Synergy (Coasys/AD4M) is early-stage [a] — a working prototype and whitepaper exist, but no large-scale real-world cooperative has yet run it at production scale.
governanceRequirements: Requires a cooperative structure with agreed rules for Proof-of-Integration (multi-agent co-signing) among members.
resourceRequirements: AD4M/Holochain infrastructure and a cooperative community willing to co-sign contribution claims.

name: Cybernetic non-transferable contribution credit
durability: Deliberately low — the credit decays by design, the opposite of a store of value.
portability: Not applicable — explicitly non-transferable by design.
acceptability: Not applicable — it can't be transferred, so no counterparty accepts it; a personal score, not an exchange medium.
desc: Contribution credits that decay and cannot be transferred — money abolished.
panelDesc: Replaces transferable money with a non-transferable, decaying contribution score, so accumulated power becomes structurally impossible.
g1_gamepos: Replaces the existing game; abolishes transferable money
g1_valuesignal: Single contribution score with decay; non-transferable
g1_accumulation: Prohibits accumulation by design via non-transferability + decay
g1_divisibility: The contribution score isn't a divisible quantity in the usual sense — it decays as a whole.
g1_uniformity: Non-fungible and non-transferable — the score is unique to each contributor, by design.
g2_coordination: Algorithmic-mechanism-design via central scoring system
g2_governance: Algorithmic issuance based on contribution metrics
g2_scale: Global from inception in design; replaces other systems
g3_ethic: Rousseauian; assumes contribution as default motivation
g3_accumdrive: Drive treated as artifact of transferability; designed out
g3_status: Status encoded as contribution score but non-transferable
g3_time: Short — decaying, non-transferable contribution credits with no intrinsic value, designed to force quick use.
trackRecord: The Integral Collective's contribution-credit system [a] remains a small-scale, internal experiment — no track record of use beyond its own originating community.
governanceRequirements: Requires a tightly bound collective willing to adopt non-transferable, decaying credit as its internal coordination tool — a cultural commitment, not just a technical one.
resourceRequirements: A ledger system to track decaying contribution scores; otherwise minimal infrastructure.

name: Demurrage currency
durability: Durable as a note or ledger entry, but the holding-cost design actively discourages sitting still — built to circulate, not to be hoarded.
portability: Portable within its circulation area (Chiemgauer-style), typically locally bounded like other complementary currencies.
acceptability: Narrow — accepted within its regional merchant network by design.
desc: Silvio Gesell's insight in practice: a holding fee forces money to circulate.
panelDesc: Charges a small periodic fee on idle balances, so holders are pushed to circulate money quickly instead of hoarding it — Gesell's old proposal.
g1_gamepos: Modifies the game; adds negative carry to circulate money
g1_valuesignal: Single rational unit with built-in negative carry cost
g1_accumulation: Penalizes accumulation through holding fees
g1_divisibility: Finely divisible like conventional currency — the holding fee doesn't change the unit's granularity.
g1_uniformity: Fungible — one note is interchangeable with any other; only the holding cost differs by time held.
g2_coordination: Price-aggregation with built-in carry cost driving circulation
g2_governance: Variable: community, regional authority, or bank
g2_scale: Local to regional typically; federation rare historically
g3_ethic: Smithian; carry cost disciplines self-interest
g3_accumdrive: Drive moderated through carry cost
g3_status: Partially encoded but discouraged from accumulation
g3_time: Short — the holding fee that solves unbounded accumulation does so by forcing quick circulation, orienting the mechanism short-term as a side effect.
trackRecord: The Chiemgauer has circulated in Bavaria since 2003 [a], one of the longer-running, better-documented complementary-currency deployments.
governanceRequirements: Requires an issuing association or cooperative to manage the currency and the demurrage mechanism; local merchants must opt in to accept it.
resourceRequirements: An issuing organization and a network of participating local merchants; largely paper-note-based systems need minimal digital infrastructure.

name: Distributed-ledger protocol grammar
durability: Not fixed at the protocol level — depends on which specific instrument is instantiated using the grammar.
portability: Not fixed at the protocol level, same reasoning.
acceptability: Undefined at the protocol level — acceptability belongs to the instantiated tokens, not the grammar itself.
desc: Protocol grammar for plural economic instruments — value without a common scalar.
panelDesc: A grammar for plural economic instruments rather than one currency: multiple token types, each with its own valuation index, in one protocol.
g1_gamepos: Modifies the game; substrate for plural valuation indices
g1_valuesignal: Plural units of account: working tokens, derivative tokens
g1_accumulation: Accumulation governed by protocol and community rules
g1_divisibility: Depends on the instantiated instrument — the protocol grammar fixes neither divisibility nor its opposite.
g1_uniformity: Depends on the instantiated instrument — working tokens and derivative tokens can differ in fungibility.
g2_coordination: Algorithmic-mechanism-design with plural valuation indices — a deliberately engineered protocol layer, designed top-down rather than emerging organically from participant relationships.
g2_governance: Token issuance per protocol; community-DAO governance
g2_scale: Network-scale; federation through cross-protocol composability
g3_ethic: Smithian-Rousseauian; assumes capacity for cooperative protocol design alongside ordinary self-interest.
g3_accumdrive: Drive reframed as risk-bearing rather than asset-holding
g3_status: Pluralized through multiple indices of valuation
g3_time: Variable — a protocol grammar with no common time scalar; orientation depends entirely on the token design built on top of it.
trackRecord: The ECSA protocol (Helsinki) [a] remains at research/prototype stage, with limited real-world production deployment so far.
governanceRequirements: Depends on the specific instrument instantiated using the grammar — the protocol itself doesn't fix this.
resourceRequirements: Depends on the specific instrument instantiated; the grammar itself requires development expertise to use.

name: Loan-granting closed-circuit credit
durability: Durable as ledger credit — nearly a century of continuous operation at WIR Bank.
portability: Deliberately non-portable outside the closed circuit — non-convertibility to national currency is the whole point.
acceptability: Broad within its member network (WIR Bank's Swiss SME base), zero outside it by design.
desc: Closed-circuit business credit — WIR Bank model; accumulation bounded by non-convertibility.
panelDesc: A closed-circuit business credit network using an internal unit convertible only within the circle, letting Swiss SMEs extend credit directly.
g1_gamepos: Modifies the game; peer credit within a closed circuit
g1_valuesignal: Single unit pegged to national currency; circulation-bounded
g1_accumulation: Enables accumulation but non-convertibility constrains hoarding
g1_divisibility: Finely divisible, pegged 1:1 to Swiss francs in granularity.
g1_uniformity: Fungible within the closed circuit — any WIR credit is interchangeable with any other.
g2_coordination: Bounded-trust at entry; price-aggregation within circle
g2_governance: Bank-issuer with collateral requirements; member governance
g2_scale: Regional typically; non-convertibility constrains scale
g3_ethic: Smithian; self-interest within mutual-credit bounds
g3_accumdrive: Drive accepted but non-convertibility constrains hoarding
g3_status: Encoded but circumscribed by closed-circle membership
g3_time: Variable — WIR itself has run for 90+ years and its loans amortize over years, but the closed-circuit business-credit mechanism takes no fixed position on time horizon of its own.
trackRecord: Operating continuously since 1934, WIR Bank remains one of the longest-running, best-documented mutual-credit systems in the world, still serving a substantial share of Swiss SMEs [a].
governanceRequirements: Requires membership in the WIR Bank cooperative, open to any incorporated Swiss business.
resourceRequirements: No new infrastructure — WIR credit substitutes for working capital through an existing business banking relationship.

name: Local complementary currency
durability: Durable as paper notes or ledger entries for as long as the issuing organization operates.
portability: Deliberately restricted to a local area — 'money that can only spend nearby' is the entire design intent.
acceptability: High within the local merchant network it's designed for, zero outside it.
desc: Berkshares-style local notes — money that can only spend nearby.
panelDesc: A currency pegged to the national one but spendable only within a defined area, keeping money circulating among nearby independent businesses.
g1_gamepos: Modifies the game; circulation anchored to local economy
g1_valuesignal: Single rational unit, often pegged to national currency
g1_accumulation: Enables accumulation but local-only spendability constrains hoarding
g1_divisibility: Finely divisible, typically pegged to the national currency it complements.
g1_uniformity: Fungible within its local network — any note is interchangeable with any other.
g2_coordination: Bounded-trust within locale; price-aggregation against fiat reference
g2_governance: Local issuing organization or municipal authority
g2_scale: Local by design; federation through complementary currency networks
g3_ethic: Smithian; local community as trust anchor
g3_accumdrive: Drive accepted but local-only spendability constrains hoarding
g3_status: Encoded but localized to community
g3_time: Short — no actual architectural connection to a durable good; local circulation alone doesn't establish one.
trackRecord: BerkShares (Massachusetts) and the Bristol Pound (UK) [a] both ran for over a decade with real circulation, though the Bristol Pound wound down its currency operations in 2021 amid declining usage.
governanceRequirements: Requires an issuing nonprofit or municipal-backed organization and a network of participating local merchants.
resourceRequirements: An issuing organization and local merchant buy-in; typically backed 1:1 by national-currency reserves held by the issuer.

name: Mutual credit clearing
durability: Not a stored value at all — balances are running ledger positions, not a token that changes hands.
portability: Bounded to network members — balances only exist within the specific trust network (Sardex-style), not portable outside it.
acceptability: High within the specific business network, zero outside it — participation IS the acceptability boundary.
desc: Sardex-style peer credit clearing — sum of balances always zero.
panelDesc: Every transaction credits one account and debits another by the same amount, so the network's total balance is mathematically always zero.
g1_gamepos: Modifies the game; peer-to-peer credit extension
g1_valuesignal: Single unit, often pegged to national currency for clarity
g1_accumulation: Sum of balances is zero; net accumulation impossible by design
g1_divisibility: Finely divisible, usually denominated to match national-currency precision for clarity.
g1_uniformity: Fungible — each unit of clearing credit is interchangeable; only the zero-sum balance rule differs.
g2_coordination: Bounded-trust mutual; peer-to-peer credit extension
g2_governance: Third-party ledger keeper; member-collective governance
g2_scale: Regional typically; federation through nested credit commons
g3_ethic: Rousseauian; assumes capacity for mutual trust
g3_accumdrive: Drive structurally limited; net accumulation impossible
g3_status: Separated from monetary signal; recognition through trust extension
g3_time: Variable — a peer-credit clearing substrate whose orientation depends entirely on credit-limit and settlement rules, not a fixed design choice.
trackRecord: Sardex has operated in Sardinia since 2010 [a], clearing a meaningful volume of business-to-business trade annually among several thousand member companies.
governanceRequirements: Requires a clearing-network operator (a company or cooperative) to admit members, set credit limits, and manage the zero-sum ledger.
resourceRequirements: Membership in the specific clearing network; no separate capital reserve since balances net to zero across the network.

name: Mutual-credit-on-blockchain
durability: Durable as an on-chain ledger entry, inheriting blockchain persistence.
portability: Portable within its trust-graph network; UBI-minting variants still bound acceptance to graph membership.
acceptability: Narrow — accepted within the specific trust-graph a user is connected to, not universal even within the platform.
desc: Mutual credit ported to a trust-graph chain; Circles adds UBI minting.
panelDesc: Ports mutual-credit accounting onto a blockchain trust graph; some versions also mint a small universal basic income directly to participants.
g1_gamepos: Modifies the game; mutual credit substrate plus crypto-native features
g1_valuesignal: Single unit per network; some designs add UBI minting
g1_accumulation: Varies by design: pure mutual credit zero-sum; Circles adds minting
g1_divisibility: Finely divisible on-chain, same precision as any standard fungible token.
g1_uniformity: Fungible within a given trust-graph network, though UBI-minting variants add per-issuer complexity.
g2_coordination: Bounded-trust plus algorithmic-mechanism-design
g2_governance: Per-account or per-trust-edge issuance; protocol-level rules
g2_scale: Global potential; federation through trust-graph topology
g3_ethic: Smithian-Rousseauian; mutual credit assumes capacity for communal trust among members, run through crypto-native infrastructure that still presumes ordinary self-interest at the edges.
g3_accumdrive: Drive limited by mutual credit logic; some designs add minting
g3_status: Separated through trust-graph topology
g3_time: Variable by design — mutual credit plus optional UBI minting, with no fixed time orientation of its own.
trackRecord: Circles UBI has run live on-chain since 2020 [a], with a substantial registered user base, though actual active daily use remains a small fraction of registrations.
governanceRequirements: Requires joining a trust graph — users must be vouched for by existing members; no central authority, but real social coordination is needed to bootstrap trust.
resourceRequirements: A blockchain wallet and gas fees to interact with the network; no capital requirement to receive the UBI issuance itself.

name: Programmable-layer digital commodity currency
durability: High — as durable as the network's continued operation, running without interruption since 2015.
portability: Fully portable — a private key moves any amount anywhere instantly, same as Bitcoin.
acceptability: Broad within crypto/DeFi and growing institutional use, though narrower than fiat.
desc: Sovereign issuance replaced; programmable layer enables plural economic systems atop one base currency.
panelDesc: A programmable settlement layer whose native token also pays for computation, letting other monetary systems be built atop one base currency.
g1_gamepos: Replaces sovereign issuance; adds a programmable execution layer on which plural economic systems can be built
g1_valuesignal: Single unit serving dual roles — store of value and computation fuel (gas); demand-driven alongside engineered scarcity
g1_accumulation: Variable; staking yields accrue to validators while EIP-1559 burns base fees; net supply is policy-adjustable, not hard-capped
g1_divisibility: Divisible to 10^18 wei per ETH — extremely fine-grained, engineered precision.
g1_uniformity: Fungible as a store of value, though its dual role as gas can make specific ETH functionally 'spent' differently.
g2_coordination: Algorithmic-mechanism-design: proof-of-stake consensus, EIP-1559 fee market; active protocol governance through the EIP process
g2_governance: Ethereum Foundation and developer community govern through EIPs; no single issuer; validators participate in consensus
g2_scale: Global from inception; L2 rollups extend throughput without native federation logic at the base layer
g3_ethic: Smithian by default; the base layer imposes no single anthropological assumption — the ecosystem built atop hosts diverse value systems, so the taxonomy's default reading applies.
g3_accumdrive: Drive enabled through appreciation and staking yields; moderated relative to Bitcoin by variable supply policy and staking participation requirement
g3_status: Partially encoded in monetary signal; pluralized through the ecosystem of tokens, DAOs, and applications built atop the base layer
g3_time: Variable — a general-purpose programmable layer with no fixed time-orientation of its own; what’s built on it decides.
trackRecord: Continuously operating since 2015 [a], now the second-largest cryptocurrency by market capitalization and the base layer for most DeFi and NFT activity — extensively documented real-world use.
governanceRequirements: None to hold or transact; protocol governance happens through a rough-consensus process among client developers, researchers, and node/validator operators, outside any individual user's control.
resourceRequirements: A wallet and ETH for gas fees; running a validator node requires 32 ETH in stake plus reliable infrastructure.

name: Open value accounting
durability: Contribution records persist on the ledger, but the value they represent is periodically re-weighted by democratic agreement — durable record, revisable valuation.
portability: Bound to the specific network's ledger (Sensorica-style); contributions don't transport to other networks.
acceptability: Narrow — accepted only within the specific value-network it was earned in.
desc: Sensorica-style ledgers of contribution across multiple value registers.
panelDesc: Tracks contributions across multiple weighted registers — time, expertise, capital — then allocates equity-shares by democratic agreement.
g1_gamepos: Modifies the game; tracks contributions across multiple registers
g1_valuesignal: Multiple contribution types weighted by democratic agreement
g1_accumulation: Accumulation in equity-shares rather than spendable currency
g1_divisibility: Contribution types aren't a divisible common scalar — each register is valued on its own terms.
g1_uniformity: Non-fungible — multiple distinct contribution types, weighted by democratic agreement rather than interchangeable.
g2_coordination: Deliberative with peer review under social charter
g2_governance: Network-collective; democratic weighting of contributions
g2_scale: Network-scale; cross-network federation through value transfer
g3_ethic: Rousseauian; gift-economy plus market integration
g3_accumdrive: Drive reframed through equity-share rather than spendable currency
g3_status: Separated through multiple contribution registers
g3_time: Variable — allocation depends on the network’s own governance choices about which registers matter, not a fixed orientation.
trackRecord: Sensorica (Montréal) has used open value accounting since around 2011 for its own hardware-development projects [a] — a real, sustained, but small-scale deployment.
governanceRequirements: Requires a network with agreed rules for weighting and valuing different contribution types — typically democratic/consensus-based among network participants.
resourceRequirements: A ledger system to track contributions across multiple registers; no capital reserve required.

name: Quadratic funding
durability: Not applicable — matching funds are distributed and consumed each round, not held as a durable store.
portability: Not applicable — the mechanism allocates an existing pool, it doesn't produce a portable unit of its own.
acceptability: Not applicable — there's no unit counterparties accept; it's an allocation algorithm, not a medium of exchange.
desc: Gitcoin-style matching that weighs the breadth of small donors over big checks.
panelDesc: Weighs the number of contributors to a cause more heavily than any single donation's size, favoring broad grassroots support in matching funds.
g1_gamepos: Modifies the game at the public-goods allocation layer
g1_valuesignal: Single matching-fund unit; algorithm weights breadth over depth
g1_accumulation: Accumulation by recipients; mechanism limits funder dominance
g1_divisibility: The matching-fund unit is finely divisible, same precision as the underlying currency it is denominated in.
g1_uniformity: Fungible — every matching-fund unit is interchangeable; the algorithm weights count of contributors, not the unit itself.
g2_coordination: Algorithmic-mechanism-design in service of deliberative aim
g2_governance: Sponsor funds matching pool; protocol weights contributions
g2_scale: Round-scale typically; federation through cross-round composability
g3_ethic: Smithian-Rousseauian; individual preference signaling (self-interested) aggregated for a collective, civic purpose.
g3_accumdrive: Drive partially redirected; funder dominance limited algorithmically
g3_status: Partially separated; breadth-of-support weights over depth
g3_time: Variable — orientation depends entirely on the funded project's own horizon, not a property of the funding mechanism itself.
trackRecord: Gitcoin Grants has run dozens of quadratic-funding rounds since 2019 [a], distributing substantial matching funds to open-source and public-goods projects — one of the most-used mechanisms in this dataset.
governanceRequirements: Requires a matching-pool sponsor (a foundation, protocol treasury, or similar) and a platform to run the rounds; individual contributors need no special structure.
resourceRequirements: A matching-fund pool and a quadratic-funding platform (e.g. Gitcoin's own, or open-source alternatives like Allo Protocol).

name: Recursive mutual credit protocol
durability: Inherits whatever durability property the parent network's units have — the protocol itself doesn't fix this.
portability: Portable across the federated network of nested mutual-credit groups, but not outside that federation.
acceptability: Bound to whichever network(s) federate under the protocol — narrow relative to fiat, potentially broad within a large federation.
desc: Meta-protocol: mutual credit networks nesting recursively.
panelDesc: A meta-protocol letting independently governed mutual-credit networks nest inside one another recursively, inheriting a parent network's rules while federating by design.
g1_gamepos: Modifies the game; meta-protocol for nesting credit networks
g1_valuesignal: Inherits parent network's units; supports plural sub-units
g1_accumulation: Inherits parent network's accumulation regime; supports plural
g1_divisibility: Inherits the parent network's divisibility — the meta-protocol doesn't fix this itself.
g1_uniformity: Inherits the parent network's fungibility, while supporting plural sub-units across federated networks.
g2_coordination: Bounded-trust mutual at each node; recursive at protocol level — coordination emerges organically from bilateral trust relationships between account-holders, not from a top-down designed mechanism layer.
g2_governance: Per-ledger governance; protocol-level rules for nesting
g2_scale: Designed for recursive federation; scales through nesting
g3_ethic: Smithian by default; inherits whichever parent network's assumptions it's federated with, with no signal of its own pointing elsewhere — the taxonomy's default reading applies.
g3_accumdrive: Inherits parent network's accumulation regime
g3_status: Inherits parent network's status logic
g3_time: Variable — inherits whatever time-preference orientation its parent network encodes; it has none of its own.
trackRecord: The Credit Commons Collective's protocol [a] remains early-stage — a specification and reference implementation exist, but widescale federation of mutual-credit networks under it hasn't yet occurred.
governanceRequirements: Requires each participating mutual-credit network to agree to the federation protocol's rules for inter-network settlement.
resourceRequirements: Existing mutual-credit network infrastructure willing to federate; the meta-protocol itself adds coordination overhead, not new capital requirements.

name: Retroactive public goods funding
durability: Not applicable — a one-time distribution tied to demonstrated past impact, not a durable store of value.
portability: Not applicable — the mechanism allocates an existing token (e.g. OP) after the fact, it doesn't create a portable unit.
acceptability: Not applicable — it's a distribution mechanism, not something counterparties accept in trade.
desc: Pay after the impact is visible — Optimism-style retroactive funding.
panelDesc: Funds public goods only after impact is demonstrated, with reviewers rewarding completed contributions rather than funding proposals upfront.
g1_gamepos: Modifies the game at the public-goods allocation layer
g1_valuesignal: Single matching-fund unit; allocation follows demonstrated impact
g1_accumulation: Accumulation by recipients; mechanism rewards proven contribution
g1_divisibility: The funding unit is finely divisible, matching the underlying token (e.g. OP) it is denominated in.
g1_uniformity: Fungible — funding allocations are interchangeable units, differentiated only by amount, not identity.
g2_coordination: Deliberative ex-post evaluation of demonstrated impact
g2_governance: Sponsor or DAO allocates; evaluation by selected reviewers
g2_scale: Network-scale typically; federation underdeveloped
g3_ethic: Smithian-Rousseauian; individual raters exercising a communal capacity for retrospective impact judgment.
g3_accumdrive: Drive partially redirected; reward follows demonstrated value
g3_status: Partially separated; recognition through retrospective evaluation
g3_time: Long — retroactive public-goods funding reads as institutional-stability-adjacent, rewarding sustained contribution to shared infrastructure.
trackRecord: Optimism's RetroPGF has run multiple funding rounds since 2022 [a], distributing OP tokens to public-goods projects based on demonstrated impact — a real, well-documented, growing program.
governanceRequirements: Requires a funding body (here, the Optimism Collective) with a badgeholder or similar review process to evaluate impact and allocate funds; recipients need no special structure.
resourceRequirements: An existing token/treasury to fund rounds from; recipients need only a wallet to receive funds.

name: Threshold-based flow funding
durability: Not applicable — simulation-only allocation logic, no durable token or store of value involved.
portability: Not applicable — the mechanism redistributes overflow between participants, it doesn't create a portable medium.
acceptability: Not applicable — no deployed prototype exists yet, so real-world acceptability can't be assessed.
proto: Simulation only — no deployed prototype (proposed: DAO contributor compensation, OSS funding, research-collective allocation, community grant programs)
desc: Minimum-guarantee, capped-maximum funding with recursive peer-preference redistribution of overflow.
panelDesc: Guarantees each participant a sustainable funding floor and caps individual maximums, then recursively redistributes overflow according to each participant's own allocation preferences.
g1_gamepos: Modifies the public-goods allocation layer; adds minimum-viability floors and maximum-capacity ceilings absent from quadratic funding
g1_valuesignal: Single matching-fund unit; distribution follows minimum-then-proportional-then-capped allocation logic
g1_accumulation: Enables accumulation up to a maximum threshold; overflow beyond the cap is recursively redistributed, penalizing concentration
g1_divisibility: The funding unit is finely divisible, following the minimum-then-proportional-then-capped allocation logic.
g1_uniformity: Fungible — each unit of redistributed overflow is interchangeable.
g2_coordination: Algorithmic threshold enforcement plus participant-directed recursive redistribution of overflow
g2_governance: Protocol-defined thresholds; participants set individual allocation preferences that shape the redistribution flow
g2_scale: Tested in simulation from 10 to 1000+ accounts; designed for DAOs and decentralized communities rather than a fixed geography
g3_ethic: Smithian-Rousseauian; balances individual sustainability guarantees with collective, preference-driven redistribution.
g3_accumdrive: Drive bounded by the maximum threshold; recursive overflow redistribution channels excess rather than letting it concentrate
g3_status: Partially separated; minimum thresholds guarantee sustainability independent of accumulated status
g3_time: Long — the source design treats long-term sustainability as co-equal with allocation efficiency, a stated orientation the axis credits directly.
trackRecord: Simulation only — no deployed prototype exists yet, so there is no real-world track record to report [a] (proposed applications: DAO contributor compensation, OSS funding, research-collective allocation, community grant programs).
governanceRequirements: Would require a funding body to set the minimum/cap thresholds and administer the redistribution logic — not yet tested against a real governance process.
resourceRequirements: Would require a funding pool and a platform implementing the threshold-based allocation logic; neither has been built at production scale yet.

name: Time-based reciprocity ledger
durability: Not a stored value — hours are earned and spent as ledger entries, not a token held as a store of value.
portability: Portable within the specific timebank network (hOurworld/TimeBanks USA), not convertible outside it.
acceptability: High within its member network by design (any hour equals any hour), zero outside it.
desc: One hour = one hour regardless of skill; net accumulation impossible.
panelDesc: Values every contributor's hour identically regardless of skill, with balances netting to zero so accumulation stays structurally impossible.
g1_gamepos: Modifies the game; time as unit equalizes hourly value
g1_valuesignal: Single time-unit; one hour equals one hour regardless of skill
g1_accumulation: Sum of balances is zero; net accumulation impossible by design
g1_divisibility: Deliberately granular at the hour — 'one hour equals one hour' is the whole design point, not infinitely divisible.
g1_uniformity: Fungible in the most radical sense — an hour of any skill is interchangeable with any other hour.
g2_coordination: Bounded-trust mutual; time as common denominator
g2_governance: Network coordinator; member-collective governance
g2_scale: Local typically; federation through time-bank networks
g3_ethic: Rousseauian; assumes equality of hours across persons
g3_accumdrive: Drive structurally limited; net accumulation impossible
g3_status: Designed out through hour-equality regardless of skill
g3_time: Variable — net-zero accumulation pulls short-term, while the stated purpose of durable mutual-aid relationships pulls long-term; the mechanism itself doesn't resolve the tension.
trackRecord: TimeBanks USA and hOurworld [a] together coordinate a large number of local time-banking networks with a real, long-running (since the 1980s), if modest-scale, track record.
governanceRequirements: Requires a local timebank organization (often volunteer-run or nonprofit) to coordinate membership and record hours.
resourceRequirements: A ledger to track hours (many networks use free/low-cost software like hOurworld) and a coordinating organization; no capital reserve needed.

name: Universal basic income / dividend
durability: Inherits the issuing currency's durability entirely — UBI is a distribution rule, not a new medium.
portability: Inherits the issuing currency's portability entirely, same reasoning.
acceptability: Inherits the issuing currency's acceptability entirely — UBI changes who receives an existing medium, it doesn't create a new one.
desc: Distribution-layer modification: a baseline received by all, accumulation continues above.
panelDesc: Layers a guaranteed periodic baseline payment atop whatever currency a community uses; normal accumulation still continues above that floor.
g1_gamepos: Modifies the game at the distribution layer; pluralistic
g1_valuesignal: Inherits the issuing currency's value-signal properties
g1_accumulation: Enables accumulation but ensures floor through periodic distribution
g1_divisibility: Inherits the issuing currency's divisibility entirely — UBI is a distribution rule, not a new unit.
g1_uniformity: Inherits the issuing currency's fungibility entirely, same reasoning.
g2_coordination: Inherits issuing currency's coordination mechanism
g2_governance: Issuing authority (state, DAO, or community) sets distribution
g2_scale: Polity-scale typically; can be national or community
g3_ethic: Rousseauian; assumes universal entitlement to an economic floor — provisioning through collective contribution to group need, not individual merit or self-interest.
g3_accumdrive: Drive accepted above floor; floor ensures non-destitution
g3_status: Partially separated; everyone receives baseline regardless of status
g3_time: Variable — a policy layer atop other currencies whose orientation depends entirely on parameters like duration and inflation-adjustment, not a fixed design choice.
trackRecord: Real pilots have run in multiple places — Stockton's SEED program (2019-2021) and numerous GiveDirectly cash-transfer programs [a] have produced published results — though no country has adopted UBI as permanent, universal policy yet.
governanceRequirements: Requires a funding body (government, foundation, or NGO) to administer distribution; recipients need no special structure — this is a distribution-layer rule on an existing currency.
resourceRequirements: A funded pool of the issuing currency and a distribution mechanism (bank transfers, mobile money, etc.); recipients need only an account able to receive it.

name: Credit union / member-governed deposit
durability: Durable — member share capital and deposits persist for as long as the credit union operates, and are typically covered by the same deposit-guarantee insurance as bank accounts.
portability: Low — share capital is redeemed with the credit union rather than transferred, and membership is bound to a defined common bond (a community, an employer, or an association).
acceptability: Narrow — a deposit is a store of value and a claim on the institution, not a medium accepted in trade outside it.
desc: Members pool deposits into an institution they own and govern one-member-one-vote, regardless of how much each has put in.
panelDesc: Pools member deposits and share capital into a member-owned lender, where governance is one-member-one-vote at the AGM regardless of the size of any member’s balance — financial stake and control are deliberately decoupled.
g1_gamepos: Modifies the game; pools member deposits into member-owned credit instead of shareholder-owned banking.
g1_valuesignal: Single conventional unit of account; the departure is in who owns and governs the institution, not in the unit.
g1_accumulation: Enables accumulation but bounds it — cooperative and credit-union law typically caps the dividend payable on member share capital.
g1_divisibility: Deposits and member shares are finely denominated, like any conventional bank balance.
g1_uniformity: Fungible — a member share is an interchangeable financial unit; the one-member-one-vote right riding on it is not, but this axis tracks the unit.
g2_coordination: Deliberative member governance — one member, one vote at the AGM, regardless of the amount any member has deposited.
g2_governance: Account-holding members are the owners and elect a volunteer board one-member-one-vote regardless of capital contributed — the load-bearing difference from capped-return, which instead splits financial and governance rights into separate share classes.
g2_scale: Bound to a defined common bond — a locality, a workplace, or an association; scales through leagues and central bodies (national credit-union leagues, WOCCU) rather than by growing a single institution without limit.
g3_ethic: Smithian-Rousseauian; assumes members can hold capital in common and govern it fairly without control being proportional to the capital each contributes.
g3_accumdrive: Drive accepted but bounded — the member’s return comes as a capped dividend and better loan terms, not uncapped equity upside.
g3_status: Partially separated — a member’s economic stake and their governance voice are deliberately decoupled, so more capital never buys more votes.
g3_time: Long — credit unions build a durable institutional balance sheet held for the membership over time.
trackRecord: One of the most established mechanisms in this catalog — credit unions and cooperative banks have operated at scale for over a century across dozens of countries, under mature cooperative and mutual law [a]. The model is deliberately small-institution: in the United States the sector holds over a trillion dollars across more than 100 million members, yet the average credit union is a small fraction of the size of the average bank.
governanceRequirements: Requires incorporation as a credit union, cooperative bank, or comparable mutual under the relevant jurisdiction’s cooperative or credit-union law, with bylaws fixing one-member-one-vote governance, a defined common bond for membership, and an elected board accountable to members at an AGM.
resourceRequirements: A pooled membership large enough to fund lending from member deposits and share capital, plus the regulatory, audit, and deposit-guarantee compliance any deposit-taking institution carries.

name: Protocol-owned reserve currency
durability: Durable as long as the treasury and its smart contracts persist; the token's redemption floor is designed to only rise, but the tokenized climate assets backing the treasury carry their own verification and counterparty risk.
portability: Fully portable — a standard ERC-20 token, freely transferable and composable with other DeFi infrastructure (e.g. yield-splitting on Pendle).
acceptability: Narrow so far — accepted within the protocol's own ecosystem and the DeFi venues that list it; no independent real-world acceptance outside crypto markets confirmed.
proto: Rooted (rooted.finance) — regenerative-collateral variant; OlympusDAO and KlimaDAO are the pattern’s more-established mainnet precedents
desc: A rising-floor treasury token — Rooted backs it with climate assets instead of stablecoins.
panelDesc: Bonds and rebasing staking mint tokens against a protocol-owned treasury with a monotonically-rising price floor; Rooted's own reserve holds tokenized solar, reforestation, and other verified climate assets rather than a single stablecoin.
g1_gamepos: Modifies the game; a treasury-backed token operating within crypto-market rails rather than replacing them.
g1_valuesignal: Single rational unit; price is set by treasury-backed floor mechanics and bond pricing plus ordinary market trading, not a pure curve formula.
g1_accumulation: Enables accumulation; rebasing staking compounds automatically and the redemption floor is designed to only rise.
g1_divisibility: Finely divisible — a standard 9-decimal ERC-20 token.
g1_uniformity: Fungible — a standard interchangeable token, wrappable into a non-rebasing form for DeFi composability.
g2_coordination: Algorithmic mechanism design — treasury-valuation, bond-pricing, and automated range-stability all execute on-chain without discretionary intervention in normal operation.
g2_governance: Currently multisig-only, not an on-chain DAO — the protocol's own technical documentation describes privileged functions as gated behind a Safe multisig, with a multi-day timelock on transferring control of that multisig itself.
g2_scale: Global by design — deployed on a public L2 with no geographic binding, unlike a bioregional or local-currency architecture.
g3_ethic: Smithian; the regenerative mission is expressed through what the treasury holds — tokenized climate assets — rather than through the mechanism's own governance rules, which otherwise mirror any other market-rational, treasury-backed reserve currency.
g3_accumdrive: Drive is accepted and structurally rewarded — rebasing rewards are forfeited on early exit, and the rising floor is explicitly marketed as a savings incentive rather than a trading one.
g3_status: Emerging; the underlying architecture is proven at real scale by OlympusDAO-family deployments (with a documented history of speculative churn), but Rooted's own regenerative-collateral instance of it is still testnet-stage.
g3_time: Long by design — rebasing rewards are forfeited on exit, the redemption floor is structurally one-directional, bonds vest over a fixed period, and the protocol positions itself explicitly as a savings vehicle rather than a trading instrument.
trackRecord: Rooted itself is testnet-preview as of 2026-08 — its own site shows a testnet faucet and a "testnet preview" footer, and governance currently runs on a multisig rather than a live on-chain DAO.[a][b] The underlying protocol-owned reserve-currency ("(3,3)") pattern is proven at real scale by its originator, OlympusDAO, and by variants such as KlimaDAO — both mainnet-live for multiple years, though with a well-documented history of heavy early speculative churn and steep drawdowns rather than the purely long-horizon holding the mechanism is designed to reward. Rooted has not yet operated at that scale or duration.
governanceRequirements: A team capable of deploying and maintaining the treasury-valuation, bond, and staking contracts, plus — in Rooted's current implementation — a multisig empowered to gate privileged operations; not, at present, a live on-chain DAO.
resourceRequirements: Smart-contract deployment on a blockchain (Rooted uses Base, an Ethereum L2), initial reserve assets to seed the treasury, and — for Rooted’s specific instance — verified tokenized climate assets (solar-generation credits, reforestation credits, ecological-claim registries) to hold as reserves.

references.note: Rooted's own site — source for the treasury/bonds/staking/floor-market framing, the named climate-asset treasury holdings (Solarcoin, Treegens, Regen Network, DOVU, Klima Protocol, Crypto Endowment Network), and the testnet-preview stage (site footer, testnet faucet). The site is a client-rendered SPA that serves no content to non-JS fetchers; read via a full saved render (local/Rooted.htm, 2026-08-31) rather than a live fetch.

Rooted's own technical documentation (a static file, unlike the SPA above, and directly fetchable) — source for the governance reality (multisig-only, no on-chain DAO, per the protocol's own words), the staking/bonding contract architecture (rebasing stROOTS, a non-rebasing wstROOTS wrapper, standard + inverse bonds), the Bucky stablecoin design, and the Base deployment.

name: Stateless hard-settlement money
durability: High for the hard assets themselves — metal, livestock, and named valuables don't decay the way a paper claim or a digital balance can be erased — but the arrangement around them is fragile: the enforcement layer (kin ties, hired protection) can collapse or be displaced overnight.
portability: Mixed by design — generic metal moves easily by weight, but livestock and named valuables are cumbersome and often immobile once claimed, the same portability problem coinage historically solved for pure commodity money.
acceptability: Narrow and local — accepted only within reach of the enforcing kin, clan, or crew, or wherever the asset's physical presence and reputation can be verified in person; there is no wider institution to extend it.
proto: localized state breakdown reverting to protection rackets (warlord-checkpoint economies; mafia as private protection; 1990s Russian krysha); Somalia 1991-2006 as the fullest documented whole-economy case.
desc: When no authority enforces contracts, hard assets and paid protection are what settle every deal.
panelDesc: Where no third party enforces contracts, exchange reverts to what force and physical possession can guarantee: settlement in durable hard assets, backed by narrow-radius kin trust and, where that fails, hired protection, rather than by law.
g1_gamepos: Accepts the game; this is the Hobbesian substrate the wider market economy sits on, exposed once the Smithian layer of law and institutions is stripped away.
g1_valuesignal: Value tracks the asset itself — weighed for generic metal, individually appraised for named valuables — not a promise or a ledger entry.
g1_accumulation: Enables accumulation freely; nothing in the architecture itself brakes it — the only check is exposure to others' violence, not a rule of the system.
g1_divisibility: Coarse and lumpy — jewels, ingots, and livestock don't make change; a transaction settles in whatever unit is on hand or it doesn't happen.
g1_uniformity: Dual register — generic metal by weight is fungible, but named heirloom valuables are singular and priced individually.
g2_coordination: Narrow-radius kin, clan, or crew trust does the coordinating — there is no wider circle and no institution behind it. Across that boundary, exchange settles on the spot in hard form or it does not happen; hawala networks and diaspora reputation-credit coalitions are the co-evolved layer that extends trusted transfer and enforcement further out.
g2_governance: None, by definition — no issuer, no rule-setting body; whatever order exists is supplied informally, by kin, clan, or crew reputation and, where that fails, by paid protection.
g2_scale: Local — bounded by the reach of the enforcing group's reputation and physical presence; it does not scale past that radius without an enforcement layer of its own.
g3_ethic: Hobbesian; assumes rivalry and no guarantee of reciprocity absent enforcement — the same premise as cbdc's sovereign-discipline reading, but with the opposite remedy: no third party to enforce agreements, so exchange defaults to self-help, hard settlement, and purchased protection instead of sovereign oversight.
g3_accumdrive: Drive is accepted and unconstrained by the architecture itself — the strong accumulate freely; the only limit is exposure to others' violence, not a rule of the system.
g3_status: Encoded directly in the monetary signal — visible hard-asset holdings and the credibility of the protection behind them are the status marker; recognition does not extend past the enforcing group's own reputation.
g3_time: Medium — value rests on durable portable goods and precious metal rather than a short trading horizon, but predation and enforcement costs keep wealth from compounding across generations the way a stable long-horizon institution would allow.
trackRecord: Not a designed system — an emergent, recurring pattern rather than a launched protocol, so track record means documented recurrence, not a deployment history. Somalia's 1991-2006 stateless interval is the fullest documented whole-economy case: the pre-collapse shilling kept circulating alongside the US dollar and livestock as stores of value, hawala networks handled transfers and remittances, and local militias and clan structures supplied the enforcement a state would otherwise provide [c][d]. The same underlying pattern — protection sold in place of law — recurs in Sicilian mafia markets and in 1990s Russia's krysha ("roof") protection economy, the two most-documented non-Somali instances [a][b].
governanceRequirements: None, by definition — there's no issuer or rule-setting body to require anything of; whatever order exists is supplied informally by kin, clan, or crew reputation and, where that fails, by paid protection.
resourceRequirements: Portable hard assets to hold and defend — metal, livestock, named valuables — and the social or paid capacity to protect them: a credible ally or a credible threat, not a technology stack.

references.note: Gambetta's foundational study of the Sicilian mafia as a private-protection industry -- source for the "protection sold in place of law" framing this entry generalizes beyond Sicily. Harvard University Press, 1993/1996.
Volkov's study of 1990s Russian "violence-managing agencies" (krysha / "roof" protection) -- the modern instance named in this entry's proto. Cornell University Press, 2002.
Little's ethnographic account of Somalia's stateless economy, 1991-2006 -- source for the shilling / dollar / livestock / hawala detail in trackRecord.

Leeson's comparative study of Somalia's development indicators before and after state collapse, Journal of Comparative Economics 35(4), 2007 -- the primary quantitative source for treating Somalia 1991-2006 as a documented whole-economy case rather than an anecdote.
